1. SEO Fundamentals Learn Competition Analysis for SEO

Looking to outrank your competitors in search results? Learn how to conduct comprehensive SEO competitor analysis with expert-backed guides, free templates, and proven strategies that help you identify opportunities and close ranking gaps.

Understanding your SEO competition is crucial for developing winning strategies. Whether you’re analyzing competitor keywords, uncovering their backlink profiles, or identifying content gaps, effective competitive analysis provides the insights needed to improve your search visibility and capture more organic traffic.

This lesson brings together the most trusted SEO competitor analysis guides, templates, and resources from industry leaders like Moz, Semrush, Ahrefs and more. You’ll discover step-by-step processes for conducting competitor research, downloadable templates to streamline your analysis, and practical frameworks for turning competitive insights into actionable SEO strategies.

From identifying your true search competitors to analyzing their technical SEO strengths and content strategies, these curated resources cover every aspect of competitive SEO analysis. Start exploring below to build a systematic approach to competitor research that drives real results.

Competition Analysis FAQ

Competitive analysis in SEO is the process of examining the search engine presence, rankings, traffic and strategies of your competitors to understand their strengths and weaknesses compared to your own. This information can be incredibly valuable in forming your own SEO strategies.

Usually, the first step in any competition analysis is determining who your SEO competitors are, identifying the keywords your competitors are targeting and ranking for, analyze the structure and content of your competitors’ websites, as well as who is linking to your competitors, how many backlinks they have, the quality of these backlinks, and where they’re coming from.

Identify your real competitors, analyze their rankings, top ranked queries and ranked pages, conduct a backlink analysis, study their content strategy, review their site structure, among others. 

Your SEO competitors aren’t always your business competitors. Start by searching your target keywords in Google and identifying which sites consistently rank in top positions. Use tools like Semrush’s Organic Research or Ahrefs’ Competing Domains to find sites targeting similar keywords and audiences, regardless of their business model.

Several free tools can help with competitor analysis: Google Search (for manual SERP analysis), MozBar (for quick domain authority checks), Ubersuggest (limited free competitor insights), and Google’s Keyword Planner. For deeper analysis, most paid tools like Semrush and Ahrefs offer free trials.

Conduct a comprehensive competitor analysis quarterly, with monthly check-ins on key competitors’ content and ranking changes. For highly competitive industries or during campaign launches, increase frequency to bi-weekly monitoring of top competitors’ activities and SERP movements.

A thorough competitor analysis report should include: competitor identification and selection criteria, keyword gap analysis, content gap opportunities, backlink profile comparison, technical SEO strengths/weaknesses, site structure analysis, and actionable recommendations prioritized by potential impact.
